title: Outside morning light (limited sky)
summary: Any outdoor morning photons when trees, streets, or heavy cloud limit the view—still worth practicing over staying inside.

sections.heading: What this tier is
sections.body: Outside morning light with limited sky is the entry sunrise tier: you step outdoors near dawn even when trees, buildings, narrow streets, or heavy cloud constrain the view. Porches, tree-lined blocks, and overcast dawns belong here. It is real outdoor light—just not open-sky or horizon quality.

sections.heading: Why it still matters
sections.body: Even constrained outdoor morning light beats indoor brightness and spectrum for circadian entrainment. Showing up outside anchors timing when horizon or open-sky tiers are impossible. This guide’s tier system acknowledges limited sky as worthwhile without pretending you saw the disk through a canyon.

sections.heading: Practical habit
sections.body: Step outside in the morning. Eyes open; avoid sunglasses if safe. A short stop before indoor work helps. Skip practicing glass-through-window “outdoor” light. When weather or travel opens a park or clear horizon, upgrade to open-sky or horizon tiers.

sections.heading: What is solid vs framework
sections.body: Solid ground: any outdoor morning light is usually better than none for circadian timing. Framework: that limited-sky mornings are pointless, or that they equal horizon sunrise. They are a valid floor—not the ceiling.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Practice Outside morning light (limited sky) when that was your sunrise practice. It supports a 1.25× morning-light signal. Upgrade to open-sky or horizon when conditions allow. Read Why sunrise is the most important part of the day for the full lesson. Educational only—not medical advice.
